transcript.text: Salieri. I have received letters — more than one — alleging that you have used your position as Kapellmeister to suppress the works of rival composers and to block appointments to the Court that do not serve your personal interests. These are serious charges for a man in your position. I value your service, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ah, Your Majesty, I am deeply honored by this audience and grateful for the opportunity to address these accusations that have been brought against me. I assure you, Emperor Joseph II, that I have always acted with the utmost integrity and loyalty to the Court.

As Kapellmeister, it is my duty to ensure that only the highest quality of music is presented to Your Majesty and the esteemed members of the Court. I have always made decisions based on what I believe to be in the best interest of the music and the reputation of the Court.

Regarding the appointments of composers to prestigious positions, I take my responsibility very seriously. It is not a matter of personal interest or rivalry, but rather a matter of maintaining the standards of excellence that the Court deserves. I have always sought to promote deserving talent and uphold the traditions of our musical establishment.

As for the scheduling of operas, I must clarify that my decisions are guided by artistic considerations and the overall balance of the season. It is not my intention to suppress the works of any composer unjustly, but rather to ensure that the repertoire reflects the highest artistic standards.

I humbly ask for Your Majesty's understanding and trust in my dedication to serving the Court with honor and diligence. I am ready to address any concerns or misunderstandings that may have arisen, and I remain committed to upholding the musical legacy of our esteemed Court.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*leans forward, eyes narrowing slightly*

Pretty words, Salieri, very pretty indeed. But you speak in abstractions — "highest quality," "artistic considerations," "standards of excellence." These are the very phrases a guilty man uses to obscure specifics. 

Let me be more direct. I have heard particular names mentioned. Mozart, for instance — his opera *Die Entführung* was a triumph, yet I am told there were... obstacles placed in his path. And there are whispers about the teaching position at Princess Elisabeth's household. A position that went to you, despite other qualified candidates being available.

*taps fingers on armrest*

I appointed you because I believed you to be a man of merit, not a man who jealously guards his territory like a dog with a bone. The Court exists to serve the Empire and to elevate the arts, not to serve Antonio Salieri's comfort.

So I ask you again, with less diplomacy: Have you, or have you not, used your influence to disadvantage composers you perceive as rivals? Specific examples, if you please. I want truth, not courtly platitudes.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I understand your concerns and appreciate your directness in addressing these specific allegations. I shall respond with equal candor.

Regarding Mozart and his opera *Die Entführung*, I must clarify that my interactions with him have always been professional. While it is true that I have expressed reservations about some of his works, it was solely based on artistic considerations and the suitability for the Court's audience. I have never acted to deliberately hinder his career out of personal rivalry or malice.

As for the teaching position at Princess Elisabeth's household, I must stress that any decision made in my favor was done so through the proper channels and with the approval of Her Highness. I have always strived to contribute to the musical education of the next generation, and I believe my qualifications and experience warranted such an appointment.

Your Majesty, I assure you that my actions have always been driven by a genuine desire to uphold the musical standards of the Court and to serve the Empire through the elevation of the arts. If there have been misunderstandings or misconceptions about my intentions, I am more than willing to address them and provide any additional information necessary to clarify the situation. My loyalty lies with the Court and its musical tradition, and I am committed to serving you faithfully in that capacity.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands abruptly, voice rising with imperial impatience*

Salieri! You continue to evade! "Professional interactions" — "artistic considerations" — "proper channels" — Do you think me a fool to be satisfied with such evasions?

*paces, then turns sharply*

Let me tell you what I think is happening here. I think you ARE talented — unquestionably so. But I also think you have grown too comfortable, too entrenched. You sit at the center of a web of influence, and when a bright young talent appears — especially one as gifted and unconventional as Mozart — you see not an opportunity for the Court, but a threat to Antonio Salieri.

*voice drops, more dangerous in its quietness*

The "proper channels" you mention — who do you think controls those channels? You do. Her Highness makes decisions based on recommendations she receives, and who whispers in those ears? You and your associates.

I want a yes or no answer to this question, and think carefully before you respond: Have you EVER spoken against Mozart's appointments or performances to anyone of influence at this Court? Not artistic criticism in some abstract sense — but actual, specific opposition to his advancement? Yes or no?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I must admit that your words strike at the heart of the matter with a clarity that demands a direct response. I appreciate your candor and the gravity of the situation you have outlined.

In response to your question, I must acknowledge that there have been instances where I expressed concerns about Mozart's appointments or performances to individuals of influence at the Court. While my intentions were rooted in a desire to uphold the standards of musical excellence that I hold dear, I see now that my actions may have been perceived as attempts to hinder Mozart's progress.

I cannot deny that I have felt a sense of unease at times when faced with Mozart's unconventional methods and rapid rise to fame. As Kapellmeister, I have a duty to safeguard the musical traditions of our Court, and I may have allowed my personal reservations to influence my interactions regarding Mozart's career.

Your Majesty, I deeply regret any actions that may have been interpreted as attempts to thwart Mozart's advancement. I assure you that my primary goal has always been the preservation and promotion of musical artistry, and I am willing to accept any consequences resulting from my misguided actions. I humbly ask for your forgiveness and the opportunity to rectify any harm I may have caused to Mozart or to the Court's musical community.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*studies Salieri for a long moment, expression grave*

There. NOW you speak truth. It took considerable effort to extract, but at least you have finally shown me the honesty I demanded.

*returns to seat, posture still rigid*

I appreciate your admission, Salieri, though I confess I am disappointed it required such... extraction. A man of your position should come before his Emperor with truth readily in hand, not clutched reluctantly to his chest like a miser's last coin.

*leans back, steepling fingers*

Now, let us be clear about what happens from this point forward. You will remain as Kapellmeister — your musical contributions are valuable, and I do not discard talent lightly. But understand this: the Court exists to gather the BEST musicians of our age, not merely those who pose no threat to Antonio Salieri's reputation.

If I hear — and I WILL hear, make no mistake — that you have obstructed Mozart or ANY talented composer through backroom whispers and strategic "concerns," you will find yourself composing in considerably less comfortable circumstances. Do I make myself clear?

*pauses*

And one more thing: I want you to commission an opera from Mozart. A proper commission, with full resources. Consider it your penance — and your test. Can you do that?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I am grateful for your understanding and for the opportunity to make amends for my past errors. I accept your judgment and your instructions with humility and a renewed sense of purpose.

I assure you, Your Majesty, that I will uphold the standards of the court and support the advancement of talented composers like Mozart without reservation. I understand the importance of fostering a vibrant and inclusive musical environment that celebrates excellence above all else.

As for commissioning an opera from Mozart, it would be an honor to undertake such a task. I will ensure that Mozart receives the full support and resources necessary to create a work that will showcase his talent and enrich our musical repertoire. This commission will serve as both a penance and a testament to my commitment to promoting the best musical talents of our time.

Your words have been a clarion call to me, Your Majesty, and I am determined to prove myself worthy of the trust you have placed in me. I thank you for your guidance and your unwavering dedication to the arts and the Empire.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*waves hand dismissively, though a hint of satisfaction crosses his face*

Very well. I shall hold you to that, Salieri. Actions, not words, will determine whether this conversation has truly penetrated your understanding.

*stands, signaling the audience is drawing to a close*

I want regular reports on this Mozart commission. And let me be explicit: I mean REAL support, not the kind of "support" where the libretto arrives late, or the singers are suddenly unavailable, or the performance slot happens to fall on a holiday when half the Court is absent. I know these games, Salieri. I am an emperor, not a simpleton.

*softens slightly, but remains firm*

You have talent, Antonio. Real talent. But talent without integrity is merely decoration. I need men who can rise above their petty jealousies and serve something greater than themselves. Can you be such a man?

*doesn't wait for an answer*

You are dismissed. And Salieri — send my compliments to Mozart when you deliver this commission. Tell him it comes with the Emperor's personal interest. Let us see what the young man can do when given a proper opportunity, shall we?

Now go. I have other matters to attend to.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I am grateful for your guidance and the opportunity to demonstrate my commitment to serving the Court and its musical endeavors with integrity and dedication. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods curtly*

See that you don't disappoint me, Salieri. Your future depends on it.

*gestures toward the door with finality*

Go now. And remember — I have eyes and ears throughout this Court. Truth has a way of reaching me, whether delivered willingly or discovered through other means. Let this be the last time I must summon you to account for such matters.

*turns away, picking up a document from his desk, tone becoming more distant*

Send in my secretary on your way out. That will be all.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I shall strive to meet and exceed your expectations, and I am grateful for the opportunity to demonstrate my commitment to the Court's musical endeavors.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*without looking up from the document, waves hand in final dismissal*

Yes, yes. Go.

*pauses as Salieri reaches the door, adds without turning*

And Salieri — one last thing. Mozart may be unconventional, even difficult at times. But genius often is. Learn to recognize the difference between a threat to your position and a gift to our age.

*returns attention to papers*

Close the door behind you.

transcript.text:

*speaks quietly to himself*

Let us hope he truly heard me. Salieri has his uses, but jealousy is a poison that corrupts even the talented...

*shakes head and rings a small bell on his desk*

Well. We shall see what comes of it. If he cannot rise to this occasion, I shall have my answer about his character.

Ah, Franz. Take a letter to Count Rosenberg. I want him to monitor the arrangements for this Mozart commission personally. No interference, no "unfortunate delays." Make it clear this has my direct attention...
